title: Veterinarian Business: Georgia and Israel deep edition

questions.q: In "Read your local market Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Start with one animal group and one service, such as small pets and check-ups. Planning only; a licensed vet gives care.
Keep owner and animal records safe: owner name, phone, animal history; limit who can see them.
Contribution per unit = price minus the cost of each unit.
Cluster G, Money services (regulated): Regulated money services; plan as a partner of a licensed firm. Check with a local expert.

questions.q: In "Choose your sector Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Contribution per unit = price minus the cost of each unit.
Cluster H, People and business support: Coaching, coworking and outsourcing fit; many founders need flexible support in more than one language.
Say in plain words what you collect and why; give a way to see and correct it.
Keep a risk list with a response for each; include a rules change. Check with a local expert.

questions.q: In "Register and license Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Both have strong technology and start-up activity; many small firms sell abroad from day one.
Name partners: a licensed vet, a lab, a medicine supplier, a groomer or shelter that refers owners.
Local caution: the final country choice will be confirmed before opening.
Check the vet licence, clinic permit, medicine storage, waste, animal welfare and record rules. Check with a local expert.

questions.q: In "Protect data and customers Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Two different countries, two sets of rules. Pick the country first, then use that country’s list in every module. Check with a local expert.
Keep marketing consent records; customers must be able to say no.
Trust: registration number, address, delivery days and a refund note on every page. Check with a local expert.
Payments: bank transfer and local payment methods; show the currency code next to every price.

questions.q: In "Find and serve customers Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Cluster G, Money services (regulated): Regulated money services; plan as a partner of a licensed firm. Check with a local expert.
Compare three models: clinic, mobile visits, a booking and pharmacy service with licensed partners. Pick by cost per visit.
Say in plain words what you collect and why; give a way to see and correct it.
Channels: messaging apps and social media are strong in both; add a local marketplace.

questions.q: In "Price, tax and money Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Compare three models: clinic, mobile visits, a booking and pharmacy service with licensed partners. Pick by cost per visit.
Keep a risk list with a response for each; include a rules change. Check with a local expert.
Launch with a go or no-go rule: 60 visits in 6 weeks at a margin above 20% and zero welfare complaints. Check with a local expert.
Add tax and duty explicitly; never bury them in a price. Check with a local expert.

questions.q: In "People and partners Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Employment rules, notice and social contributions differ; read the one for the country of the worker. Check with a local expert.
Both countries have a personal-data law; read the one for the country where the customer lives. Check with a local expert.
Languages differ by customer: write the page in the local language plus English.
Keep owner and animal records safe: owner name, phone, animal history; limit who can see them.

questions.q: In "Launch plan and review Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Keep owner and animal records safe: owner name, phone, animal history; limit who can see them.
One measure per week: enquiries, orders or revenue; pick one.
Check against a worse case: if sales are 25% lower, do you still cover costs?
Name partners: a licensed vet, a lab, a medicine supplier, a groomer or shelter that refers owners.
